## Hypothesis

<2-3 sentences: what edge are we trying to capture, why does it exist>

We are trying to capture the edge from avoiding losing trades on J's loser days, specifically the two CALL loser trades on 5/07. The edge exists because the engine currently takes these trades and loses money, but a trendline break structure signal can identify when the market is in a confirmed uptrend, making bearish PUT trades (which are what the engine takes on loser days for CALLs? Wait, no.

Wait, the loser days on 5/07 are CALL trades: 
  5/07 SPY 734C x 3 -> -$45
  5/07 SPY 737C x 10 -> -$120

So the engine is taking CALL trades on these days and losing.

The CALL VETO is designed to veto CALL trades when bearish structure is confirmed.

So the hypothesis is: when bearish structure is confirmed (via a 5m-close-through-respected-ascending-support), taking CALL trades is detrimental, and vetoing them avoids losses.

## Mechanism

<concrete: what bars / indicators / state triggers entry, what's the exit logic>

The trendline_break_call_veto is triggered when the market_structure.py detects a break of an ascending support (i.e., a bearish structure signal). When this signal is active, the engine vetoes any CALL entry that would otherwise be triggered by the standard signal (e.g., vwap_continuation, bearish_rejection, etc.). The exit logic remains unchanged for any trade that is entered; the veto only affects entry.
